classification.difficultyReason: Equate two expressions for the same triangle's area and rearrange to deduce the sine rule.

content.prompt: Write down two formulas for the area of triangle $ABC$ and deduce the sine rule from those two formulas.

spec.sourceRegion: Challenge exercise question 1, triangle to the right of the instruction
spec.description: Unshaded triangle with A above, B lower left and C lower right; side labels lie outside their corresponding edges. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: BC=a, AC=b, AB=c; each lowercase side is opposite its corresponding uppercase vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: All vertex and side labels are permanent givens; no answer annotations are supplied.

answer.short:
$K=\frac12 ab\sin C$ and $K=\frac12 ac\sin B$, so $\displaystyle\frac{b}{\sin B}=\frac{c}{\sin C}$.

Equate the two area formulas and divide by the common factors.
answer.worked:
Let the area of triangle $ABC$ be $K$.

$$\begin{align*}K&=\frac12 ab\sin C\\K&=\frac12 ac\sin B\end{align*}$$

Equating these expressions gives

$$\begin{align*}\frac12 ab\sin C&=\frac12 ac\sin B\\b\sin C&=c\sin B\\\frac{b}{\sin B}&=\frac{c}{\sin C}.\end{align*}$$

This is the sine rule for the opposite pairs $(b,B)$ and $(c,C)$.
